name: Sonic Youth
label: DGC
lede: Thirty years of retuned guitars, screwdrivers jammed under strings and art-school nerve, from a downtown gallery noise festival to headlining Lollapalooza, and it ended the only way it could: when the marriage at its center did.

eras.title: A gallery, a guitar army, a name
eras.text: Thurston Moore and Kim Gordon met in 1980 at the last gig of Moore's band the Coachmen, and cycled through names like Male Bonding and Red Milk before Moore landed on Sonic Youth. Downtown New York in 1981 was all no wave and art spaces, and Glenn Branca's wall-of-guitars ensemble supplied both a guitarist and a first label.

years.h: Sonic Youth's first show: Noise Fest at White Columns
years.p: Kim Gordon, Thurston Moore and keyboardist Anne DeMarinis play the Noise Fest at the White Columns gallery in New York, using stand-in drummers for three songs.
years.xp:
Gordon later said the sound they wanted only arrived once Moore came up with the name Sonic Youth. The band had played as Male Bonding, Red Milk and the Arcadians before that.

The same festival gave them their third member: [[Lee Ranaldo|6eb1f3f8-5c5a-41c2-a390-f397a2b824a3]] was on the bill in [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]]'s electric guitar ensemble. Drummer [[Richard Edson|bf68dbc8-78ee-492d-8be9-36caddd27665]] came in soon after.

years.h: Sonic Youth EP · Neutral Records
years.p: [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]] signs Sonic Youth to his Neutral label in December 1981, and the band cuts five songs at a studio inside Radio City Music Hall. The EP drew uniformly favorable reviews from the American press.

years.h: Bob Bert replaces Richard Edson; first tour, opening for Swans
years.p: [[Richard Edson|bf68dbc8-78ee-492d-8be9-36caddd27665]] quits to play in KONK full-time. [[Bob Bert|205455ca-426d-442d-971f-01cde6dce988]] takes over and Sonic Youth goes out supporting [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]], the band they shared a rehearsal room with.
years.xp: On a second Swans tour that December, Thurston Moore kept criticizing Bert for not playing in the pocket. By the next record Bert was out and [[Jim Sclavunos|dc24f4fa-1b47-412f-891c-0f0a43664b8b]] was in.

eras.title: Loved in London, ignored at home
eras.text: The drummer seat kept turning over and the New York press shrugged, but Europe paid attention. By 1985 Sonic Youth had fallen out with Branca's label, made an American horror album with Lydia Lunch, and found the drummer who'd stay to the end.

years.h: Confusion Is Sex: louder, uglier, drummer No. 3
years.p: [[Jim Sclavunos|dc24f4fa-1b47-412f-891c-0f0a43664b8b]] drums on Sonic Youth's first album and quits within months. [[Bob Bert|205455ca-426d-442d-971f-01cde6dce988]] comes back on one condition: that he won't be fired after the tour.

years.big: Kill Yr Idols gets a new title
years.h: Sonic Youth vs. Robert Christgau and the Village Voice
years.p: A Village Voice critic pans a New York show. Kim Gordon writes the paper a scathing letter, and Thurston Moore renames the song Kill Yr Idols after the paper's music editor.
years.xp:
Gordon's letter attacked the Voice for not supporting local music. Robert Christgau answered that the paper had no obligation to support anyone.

Moore's reply was to retitle Kill Yr Idols as I Killed Christgau with My Big Fucking Dick. According to Wikipedia, the feud was later settled amicably.

years.h: Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore marry
years.p: Three years into the band, Gordon and Moore marry. The partnership at the middle of Sonic Youth lasts 27 years.

years.h: Bad Moon Rising · Homestead and Blast First
years.p: After a royalty dispute with [[Glenn Branca|7c0735b8-6444-47a3-a244-522fa7925834]], Sonic Youth's Martin Bisi-recorded Americana album comes out on Homestead in the US and Blast First in the UK. [[Lydia Lunch|74f2add6-e8b6-4323-a21b-443600379d16]] sings on the Manson-inspired Death Valley '69.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Bad Moon Rising sold 5,000 copies in the UK and was acclaimed there, while the New York press dismissed it as too arty and pretentious.

years.h: Steve Shelley of the Crucifucks joins without an audition
years.p: [[Bob Bert|205455ca-426d-442d-971f-01cde6dce988]] quits, bored after a year of playing Bad Moon Rising front to back. The band had seen [[Steve Shelley|998815d5-03bc-4228-807f-b550c07038d2]] drum with Lansing, Michigan's [[The Crucifucks|efe79e45-5dcd-4099-9438-e4aff57bbeb3]] and hired him on the spot.
years.xp: Bert and Shelley both appear in the Death Valley '69 video, a handover caught on film. Shelley stayed until the end in 2011.

eras.title: SST, Madonna and a candle
eras.text: Signing to Greg Ginn's SST made Sonic Youth the first band from the New York underground to get national attention. Three albums in three years followed, plus a joke side project about Madonna, and the run peaked with a double LP that critics still put at the top of the decade.

years.h: EVOL: Hendrix to one critic, toxic waste to another
years.p: Sonic Youth's first album for [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]]'s SST, which made it the first New York underground band to get national attention. The New York Times' Robert Palmer compared it to Jimi Hendrix; People magazine, to a toxic waste dump.

years.h: Ciccone Youth: Sonic Youth and Mike Watt cover Madonna
years.p: With ex-[[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] bassist [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]], Sonic Youth becomes Ciccone Youth, named for Madonna's surname, and cuts Into the Groove(y). Watt covers Burning Up on the flip.

years.h: Sister, a loose concept album about Philip K. Dick
years.p: Sonic Youth's Sister draws on science fiction writer Philip K. Dick's life and work, sells 60,000 copies, and becomes the band's first album in the Village Voice Pazz & Jop Top 20.

years.h: Daydream Nation: a double LP, a Gerhard Richter candle
years.p: Recorded at Greene St. in July and August 1988 for about $30,000, Sonic Youth's double album comes out on Enigma. Teen Age Riot reaches No. 20 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart, their first real airplay.
years.xp:
Engineer Nick Sansano's studio charged $1,000 a day. The band stayed up a whole night mixing the three-part Trilogy so it could be mastered the next morning. The cover is Gerhard Richter's 1983 painting Kerze (Candle).

It came second in the Voice's Pazz & Jop poll and topped the NME, Melody Maker and CMJ year-end lists. In 2005 the Library of Congress added it to the National Recording Registry.

years.h: Sonic Youth quits Enigma and signs with Geffen's DGC
years.p: Distribution problems with Enigma push the band toward a major. They sign a five-album, $300,000 deal with Geffen that guarantees full creative control, then learn it's the smaller DGC imprint.
years.xp: Thurston Moore didn't mince words about Enigma, which was distributed by Capitol. The band was disappointed to land on DGC rather than Geffen proper, but the creative-control clause held for the next eighteen years.

eras.title: Big siblings to grunge
eras.text: On a major label Sonic Youth became the older band everyone in the alternative boom looked up to. Kim Gordon talked Nirvana onto DGC, the band opened for Neil Young, and a tour film named the moment. They also lost a friend, and by 1995 they were headlining Lollapalooza.

years.h: Goo: Chuck D on Kool Thing, a Pettibon cover
years.p: Sonic Youth's DGC debut features [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]]'s [[Chuck D|88633ac3-c8e2-420f-8415-77ac56b3105f]] on Kool Thing, which Kim Gordon based on her 1989 interview with LL Cool J. Goo sold over 200,000 copies by December.
years.xp:
Gordon, a hip-hop fan, came away from the LL Cool J interview put off by his dismissal of punk and his views on women. Kool Thing reached No. 7 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart. Raymond Pettibon's cover drawing of two mods in sunglasses is based on a photo of two witnesses in the Moors murders trial.

It cost $150,000, five times Daydream Nation. Producer Nick Sansano was replaced during mixing by Ron Saint Germain, and according to Wikipedia Sansano was so hurt he wouldn't speak to the band for years.

years.h: Kim Gordon's recommendations land Nirvana on DGC
years.p: After repeated recommendations from Kim Gordon, [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] signs to DGC. That August the two bands play seven West Coast dates together, with [[Dale Crover|9b93a71b-1484-4bea-b096-f660c1161f8a]] drumming for Nirvana.

years.h: Sonic Youth opens arenas for Neil Young and Crazy Horse
years.p: Sonic Youth supports [[Neil Young|75167b8b-44e4-407b-9d35-effe87b223cf]] and Crazy Horse on the Ragged Glory tour, taking its noise into arenas in front of Young's crowds.

years.cap: 1991: The Year Punk Broke, dir. Dave Markey
years.h: Europe with Nirvana, filmed as 1991: The Year Punk Broke
years.p: From August 20 to September 1, Sonic Youth tours Ireland, the UK, Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands with [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]], playing Reading and Pukkelpop. Dave Markey films it.
years.xp: Sonic Youth is the focus of the film, with time for Nirvana, [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]], [[Babes in Toyland|41593aa1-dda6-4a5a-af87-0eebf93e3775]], Gumball and the [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]]. Several scenes spoof Madonna's tour film Truth or Dare. It opened in theaters in December 1992.

years.h: Dirty: Spike Jonze, Ian MacKaye and a song for Joe Cole
years.p: The songs 100% and JC are about the murder of Joe Cole, a friend and former [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] roadie killed in a robbery in December 1991. Spike Jonze shoots the 100% video, and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] plays on Youth Against Fascism.
years.xp: Joe Cole had been on the 1991 European tour, and 1991: The Year Punk Broke is dedicated to him. Mike Kelley made the Dirty cover art; skater Jason Lee appears in the 100% video.

years.h: Experimental Jet Set hits No. 34, and Coco is born
years.p: Sonic Youth's best US chart showing to date comes the year Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore's daughter Coco is born. With Gordon pregnant there was never a full tour, so many of the songs were never played live.
play: Experimental Jet Set, Trash and No Star

years.h: Sonic Youth headlines Lollapalooza with Hole and Pavement
years.p: Fourteen years after a gallery noise festival, Sonic Youth tops the 1995 Lollapalooza bill, with [[Hole|1dcc8968-f2cd-441c-beda-6270f70f2863]] and [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] also on the tour. That year's Washing Machine stretched the band into long improvised pieces.

eras.title: Stolen guitars and a fifth member
eras.text: Sonic Youth spent the late 1990s doing whatever it liked: cartoon cameos, a private label for improvised records, and a fifth member from Chicago's experimental scene. Then someone drove off with their instruments, and a band built on custom tunings had to start over.

years.h: Sonic Youth plays itself on The Simpsons' Homerpalooza
years.p: In the Homerpalooza episode Sonic Youth appears as itself, and its version of The Simpsons Theme plays over the end credits.

years.h: The SYR series: improvised records on the band's own label
years.p: Sonic Youth starts SYR, its own imprint for experimental records, with titles and liner notes in a different language each time. SYR3 (1998) is titled in Esperanto and features [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]].

years.h: Almost 30 guitars stolen from Sonic Youth's van in Orange County
years.p: On Independence Day, thieves take Sonic Youth's instruments and stage gear from its tour van in Orange County, California. Some pieces turned up over the next 13 years.
years.xp:
The loss hit harder than it would most bands. Thurston Moore and Lee Ranaldo built their songs on custom tunings, often one guitar per song or two, and toured with dozens of instruments. Losing them meant losing the setups.

The band rebuilt with new gear for the Jim O'Rourke-produced NYC Ghosts & Flowers (2000). When some of the stolen instruments came back, the band went back to older material on Rather Ripped.

years.h: Jim O'Rourke becomes Sonic Youth's fifth member
years.p: Chicago producer and multi-instrumentalist [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]], already on SYR3, joins on bass, guitar and keyboards.

years.h: Murray Street, first album with Jim O'Rourke as a member
years.p: Named for the street of their downtown New York studio, Murray Street is Sonic Youth's first record with [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] as an official member. The same year the band plays the first All Tomorrow's Parties festival.

years.h: Kim Gordon, Thurston Moore and daughter Coco on Gilmore Girls
years.p: Gordon and Moore appear in the season six finale of Gilmore Girls, playing an acoustic What a Waste with their daughter Coco.

years.h: Jim O'Rourke leaves; Pavement's Mark Ibold joins
years.p: [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] leaves for film work and other projects. [[Mark Ibold|003db9eb-2a01-4ece-a5e0-87000aa502d7]] of [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]], who had played with Kim Gordon in Free Kitten, comes in on bass.

years.h: Rather Ripped, Sonic Youth's Parallel Lines
years.p: Thurston Moore wrote simpler songs, inspired by [[Blondie|4d2956d1-a3f7-44bb-9a41-67563e1a0c94]]'s Parallel Lines. On June 13, 2006, Sonic Youth plays CBGB for the first time since 1992.
years.xp: The Destroyed Room, a B-sides set that December, was Sonic Youth's final Geffen release.

years.h: Sonic Youth leaves Geffen and signs to Matador
years.p: Unhappy with how Geffen promoted its last several albums, Sonic Youth ends the relationship after the Starbucks-issued Hits Are for Squares and signs with Matador Records.

eras.title: Matador, then the end of a marriage
eras.text: Back on an indie, Sonic Youth made its highest-charting album ever. Two years later Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore separated, and a band that had always called itself a democracy couldn't function without its founding couple.

years.h: The Eternal · Matador, Sonic Youth's highest US chart peak
years.p: Recorded in Hoboken with John Agnello in late 2008, Sonic Youth's only Matador studio album reaches No. 18 on the Billboard 200. [[John Fahey|95bb27d2-43c7-4a92-85ee-f95a245f0ee4]] painted the cover.
years.xp: It was Mark Ibold's first studio album with the band. Thurston Moore said Ibold locked in immediately and knew the songs better than the rest of them. Sacred Trickster and Antenna were the singles.

years.h: Kim Gordon and Thurston Moore separate after 27 years
years.p: Gordon and Moore announce their separation. Gordon later wrote that it followed her finding out about Moore's affair with Eva Prinz, whom he married in 2020.
years.xp:
Gordon confronted Moore about a text message from another woman, according to Wikipedia's account of her memoir. Their divorce was finalized in April 2013.

Moore later moved to London with Prinz. He has said the band was a democracy of sorts and couldn't function while he and Gordon worked things out.

years.cap: SWU Music & Arts Festival, Paulínia, Brazil
years.h: The last Sonic Youth show: SWU festival, Paulínia, Brazil
years.p: A month after the separation, Sonic Youth plays its final concert at the SWU Music & Arts Festival in Paulínia, São Paulo. Lee Ranaldo then says the band is ending for a while.
years.xp: Kim Gordon opens her 2015 memoir Girl in a Band on that last night in Brazil. The band's score for the French film Simon Werner a Disparu, issued as SYR9 in 2011, was its last official release of new music.

eras.title: Let it rest in peace
eras.text: Nobody announced a breakup, and nobody needed to. Lee Ranaldo asked in 2013 that the band be left to rest in peace, Thurston Moore called it a hiatus, and instead of a reunion came memoirs, a Bandcamp archive of live shows and a 2022 rarities set, In/Out/In.

years.h: Kim Gordon's Girl in a Band calls it a split for good
years.p: Gordon's memoir Girl in a Band covers her art life, the band and the marriage, and refers several times to Sonic Youth having split up for good.

years.h: Thurston Moore publishes Sonic Life
years.p: Doubleday publishes Moore's memoir Sonic Life, his side of the story from Connecticut to downtown New York to the end of the band.
